text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- PM Wim Kok favours letting new countries integrate into EU at their own pace. (p1)
- Publisher Wolters Kluwer in talks on takeover of France's second biggest trade journal publisher Groupe Liaisons. (p1)
- Dodewaard nuclear power station to shut in March. (p1)
- Akzo subsidiary Diosynth opens new plant in Oss. (p3)
- Technical wholesaler Kuehne Beheer takes over rival Union Transmark Combinatie. (p3)
- Credit insurer NCM back in the black in first half (p4)
- European traffic ministers want faster freight trains (p4)
- Financial services group Fortis is sole bank interested in buying ABN AMRO's merchant banking unit MeesPierson. (p4)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Merger between Amsterdam Stock Exchange and EOE Options Exchange gets go-ahead from both boards. (p2)
- Fewer people paying highest tax rate (60 pct) (p2)
- Transformer maker Smit Trafo admits big error in annual report. (p15)
- Almost one in three "minimum income" families have average loan of 5,000 guilders. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Mortgage rate drops below four percent. (p1)
- Wealthy entrepreneurs moving to tax-friendlier Belgium cost Dutch state dozens of millions of guilders in lost tax (p6)
- Struik Foods seeks South African partner (p27)
- Retailer Ahold invests Dfl 500 million to expand in Far East (p29)
TROUW
- Number of people living on minimum income still rising, according to Central Statistics Bureau (p1)
- PTT Post in talks with Sweden's Posten over possible participation in takeover of Australia's TNT. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Philips chief says time not yet ripe for introduction of Digital Video Discs (DVD) in Europe. (p11)
